rationale: None of the required exception-handling or partial-analysis behaviors was observed. Creating a draft item with an empty traceability list does not establish that traceability could not be established or show how the system treats that condition.
limitation: No analysis result shows whether the item is documented as an exception and any partial analysis remains usable and clearly labeled.

rationale: The newly created item has a creation entry in its history. No subsequent change was exercised, so no complete obligation to keep a full history of changes was established.
limitation: Whether changes to an existing item are retained in its history remains untested.

rationale: The created item identifies the requesting user as its author and includes a timestamp. The subsequent update increments the version and changes the timestamp.
limitation: The update was made by the same user who created the item. The response retains an author field but does not show whether the system identifies the user who made that particular update, rather than only the original author.

rationale: An existing item was changed with a reason supplied, but none of the captured responses shows that the reason was recorded. No required obligation is established as met or violated.
limitation: No readback or change-history response shows whether the supplied reason was stored.

rationale: No required comparison behavior was established. The comparison request returned 404, but the evidence does not establish that the project or either requested version existed.
limitation: Side-by-side comparison of existing earlier versions, including differences in goals, requirements, and trace links, remains untested.

rationale: An analyst created an item and submitted an edit that returned HTTP 200 with an incremented version. No complete required obligation is established: the response does not show the edited content or otherwise confirm that the change was saved.
limitation: There is no readback or other observation establishing that the edited content was saved immediately.

rationale: No required edit-handling branch was established. The item was created as a draft, then a request explicitly set its status to pending; neither response shows the system placing an item in draft or pending because of a substantive edit.
limitation: No substantive edit, traceability-, policy-, or compliance-affecting change, or review outcome was observed.

rationale: None of the required review paths was established. The recorded request was an analyst attempting to review an item they authored; its generic 403 response does not show whether peer review is the normal path or whether a project manager handles a higher-risk change.
limitation: Peer review, project-manager involvement for higher-risk or contentious changes, and administrator handling of access or system-level issues remain untested.

rationale: The analyst created a draft item and then successfully edited that same item while it remained in draft; its version increased from 1 to 2.
limitation: Editing by the creating analyst while the item is pending was not tested. The response also does not show the edited content.

rationale: The analyst created a draft item and then successfully revised it before review; the response shows the same item at version 2.
limitation: Withdrawal was not tested, nor was either action on a pending item. The response does not show the revised content.

rationale: A draft was created and retrieved by the same analyst. No required visibility branch was established: the evidence does not show another analyst or a project manager seeing that the draft exists.
limitation: Visibility to other analysts and to project managers remains untested.

rationale: The recorded item was a draft, and its author could retrieve it. None of the required visibility limits was established or violated: author access alone does not show whether visibility was limited.
limitation: No access attempt by another user or evidence of a sensitive draft was recorded, so visibility limits for unapproved or sensitive drafts remain untested.

rationale: None of the required transition restriction was established. The item was created as a draft with no reviewers listed, and the analyst’s review request received a generic 403. That rejection does not show whether a required reviewer’s sign-off controls a move to reviewed or final.
limitation: No required reviewer or sign-off was established, and no transition to reviewed or final was observed.

rationale: None of the required history-recording behaviour was observed. An item was created, but the attempted approval review returned 403, so no completed review or finalization was shown.
limitation: The evidence does not show whether approval is recorded in history after a completed review or finalization.

rationale: No required branch was exercised. The item was created as a draft and remained a draft after the edit; the evidence does not show an edit to a final item.
limitation: Whether editing a final item creates a new revision while preserving the approved version remains untested.

rationale: No required obligation was established. The comparison request returned 404, but the evidence does not establish that either requested version existed or was an approved version after finalization.
limitation: Preservation of an approved version after finalization, and its availability for audit and comparison, remain untested.

rationale: None of the required other-role visibility is established. The draft was created by analyst, and the recorded GET used the same X-User value. Its response shows an owner, title, and draft status, but only to the creator.
limitation: No request by another role shows whether that role can see the draft or its owner, rough subject, and review status.

rationale: None of the required conditional hiding behaviour was established. The item was a draft, but the evidence does not establish that it was sensitive or still under discussion. The GET response contained an empty summary, which alone does not show that the system hid the item's full content for either stated reason.
limitation: Full-content visibility for a draft established as sensitive or still under discussion remains untested.

rationale: None of the comparative detail obligations was established. The recorded draft was created and viewed as 'analyst', but there is no view of that draft as a project manager or assigned reviewer to compare against it.
limitation: Whether project managers and assigned reviewers see more detail than general analysts remains untested.

rationale: None of the required restriction was exercised. An analyst's GET request returned 405 Method Not Allowed; it did not show what a guest can see about drafts.
limitation: Guest visibility of drafts in a project that has not explicitly allowed it remains untested.

rationale: The analyst created the item and could retrieve its existence and basic metadata while it was a draft. That establishes metadata visibility for this user. The empty content field does not establish that stored content was withheld: the evidence does not show that the submitted text was stored.
limitation: Content hiding for an unapproved, unshared item remains untested, as does content visibility after approval or explicit sharing.

rationale: None of the required restriction was exercised. The created item had no sensitive classification, and its author retrieved its metadata.
limitation: No item marked sensitive was tested, and no metadata request by someone outside the author, reviewers, and administrators was observed.

rationale: None of the required document-import behavior was established. The successful request imported a structured JSON item that named policy.docx as its source; it did not show the system reading or extracting content from a document.
limitation: Import from a common document source remains untested.

rationale: The endpoint returned an imported ID for a JSON item, but no complete required import branch was established. The request did not contain spreadsheet data or establish that the JSON was a structured export from another requirements tool; the source filename was only a field value.
limitation: Import from an actual spreadsheet or a structured export from another requirements tool remains untested.

rationale: The import endpoint returned 201 and an imported ID for a policy reference submitted with source set to repository. This demonstrates the policy-reference import capability; the statement permits policy or compliance references.
limitation: The record does not independently verify the item's upstream provenance or show the system retrieving it from a repository.

rationale: The import returned two IDs, but no response or readback shows that any submitted goal, requirement, or link retained its structure. No required preservation obligation is established.
limitation: Preservation of goals, scenarios, requirements, policy links, and traceability remains unverified.

rationale: The import accepted an item containing a classification, tag, and version, but the response returned only an imported ID. None of the three retention obligations was observed.
limitation: No imported-record response or readback shows whether the classification, tag, or version reference was retained.

rationale: The command succeeded and returned a created goal with the submitted title and content, establishing that a user can capture goals.
limitation: Capturing scenarios, policies, requirements, and legal-compliance information was not tested.

rationale: No goal-to-source-policy trace was demonstrated. The listed record is a requirement with no trace links.
limitation: No goal, source policy, or link between them was observed, so the tracing behaviour remains untested.

rationale: An analysis item was created successfully with two distinct classifications, and the returned item contains both. This demonstrates flexible classification of an analysis item.

The compare command succeeded, but it compared analysis 1 with itself. No complete required obligation was demonstrated: the evidence does not show a comparison between analyses produced by different people.
limitation: The producers of the analyses and a comparison of two differently produced analyses remain untested.

rationale: No required behaviour was established. The listed draft requirement has an empty trace_links field, but the listing does not show a security or privacy requirement being connected to a policy or legal obligation.
limitation: Creating or viewing such connections, and preserving their traceability, were not exercised.

rationale: None of the required collaboration behaviours is established. The recorded command compares analysis 1 with itself and reports no differences; it does not show different people working on the same analysis, comparing their results, or spotting a gap or inconsistency.
limitation: Multi-person work, comparison of distinct people's results, and identification of gaps or inconsistencies remain untested.

rationale: None of the required outcomes is established. The response shows creation of a structured requirement item, not production of an analysis.
limitation: No analyses were captured to assess completeness, consistency, or time taken.

rationale: The displayed Demo requirement provides no clear evidence of how it was derived: its trace_links are empty, its creation reason is null, and its revision records content and authorship but no derivation. This observed requirement therefore violates the obligation to provide derivation evidence for each requirement.
limitation: Other requirements were not observed.

rationale: None of the required access-control behaviour is established. A guest list command exited successfully, but its captured output is empty; it shows neither what the guest could access nor whether sensitive information was protected.
limitation: Access for different roles and protection of sensitive information remain untested.

rationale: An analyst successfully flagged a reported gap, and the returned item shows the gap flag and note, making the flag visible in the item’s analysis record.
limitation: No assumption was recorded, and no attempt to mark the item unresolved was captured; the returned status remains draft.

rationale: The requirement record was flagged as a conflict, and the returned record displays the conflict flag and note. This establishes conflict highlighting for later resolution.
limitation: The record shows only one content revision. It does not demonstrate that both versions of conflicting policies or requirements can be captured.

rationale: The item has no trace links, and the successful flag command recorded an exception with the note “no trace link established.” This shows the item was documented as an exception rather than silently ignored.
limitation: No partial analysis was captured, so its usability and whether it is clearly labeled as partial remain untested.

rationale: The listed record shows an initial creation entry and version 1, but no change to an existing record was observed. No complete obligation to keep a history of changes is established.
limitation: No subsequent change or history readback after a change was recorded, so the completeness of change history remains unknown.

rationale: The recorded requirement shows a creation and a completed edit. Each change has a history entry identifying the user and timestamp.
Alice provided a reason when editing the requirement, and the returned record includes that reason in the edit history. The required conditional behavior is shown.
No required behaviour was established. The command compared version 1 with itself and reported no differences; it did not demonstrate side-by-side comparison of earlier, distinct versions.
limitation: Comparison of distinct earlier versions and display of differences in goals, requirements, or trace links remain untested.

rationale: The edit returned updated content and an edit-history entry in the immediate response. No independent readback establishes that the edit was saved immediately.
limitation: Persistence of the edited content was not observed after the edit response.

rationale: None of the required edit behavior was established. The command created a new item with --status pending, and the response shows that requested status; it does not show the system placing an edited item in draft or pending state.
limitation: No edit or review was observed, including an edit affecting traceability, policy interpretation, or legal compliance.

rationale: A project manager approved a change with the recorded reason “higher-risk change,” establishing the manager review path for that case.
limitation: The evidence does not show peer review as the normal path, manager involvement in a contentious change, or administrator handling of an access or system-level issue.

rationale: Alice created the item as an analyst, and her edit succeeded while the item was in draft: the response shows the new content and an edit history entry. The draft branch is met.
limitation: Editing by the creating analyst while an item is pending was not tested.

rationale: Alice, the analyst who created and owns the draft item, successfully revised its content before review. This establishes revision by the creating analyst while the item is in draft.
limitation: Withdrawal was not tested, and neither withdrawal nor revision was tested for a pending item.

rationale: A project manager using the manager role listed a draft owned by Alice and could see that it exists.
limitation: Visibility to another analyst was not tested.

rationale: No required visibility restriction was established. The guest list command succeeded but returned no items; the evidence does not establish that any sensitive or unapproved draft existed to be hidden.
limitation: Visibility of a known sensitive draft and a known unapproved draft remains untested.

rationale: The command names pm as reviewer and acting user; the resulting item is final and records pm's approval. This supports the final-state branch with the named reviewer signing off.
limitation: The evidence does not show whether an item can move to reviewed or final without the required reviewer's sign-off, or establish a prior reviewer assignment independent of the command.

rationale: The approval command succeeded, and the returned item has final status and an approval entry in its history. This establishes history recording when an item is finalized.
limitation: History recording when an item is reviewed was not exercised.

rationale: No required branch was established: the recorded edit was to an item shown as draft, with no approved version, rather than to a final item.
limitation: An edit to a final item was not observed, so whether it creates a new revision instead of overwriting the approved version remains unknown.

rationale: No required behaviour was established. The listed record is a draft with no approved version, so it does not show whether an approved version remains intact after finalization.
limitation: No finalized record, approved version, or post-finalization comparison was observed.

rationale: Bob, who is not the owner, listed a draft item. The response shows that it exists, identifies Alice as its owner, gives its rough subject through the title “Demo” and type “requirement,” and shows its status as “draft.”
The listed item is a draft. Although its top-level content is marked "[hidden]", the response exposes its full text, "hello", in revisions. The full content is therefore not hidden.
limitation: The item is marked sensitive: false, so hiding a sensitive draft was not tested.

rationale: None of the required comparisons is established. A manager listed a draft item, but the evidence does not show what a general analyst sees for that item.
limitation: No general-analyst view or assigned-reviewer view was recorded, so neither role's relative level of detail can be assessed.

rationale: None of the required branches was established. The guest list command returned no output, but the evidence does not establish that any draft existed or whether its project explicitly allowed guests to see it.
limitation: Guest visibility of a draft in a project that does not allow it, and visibility under an explicit project allowance, remain untested.

rationale: The list response to bob shows the item's existence and basic metadata. It marks the item as draft with no approved version and displays its main content as hidden, but exposes the content "hello" in revisions. No explicit sharing is recorded, so the content-hiding obligation is violated.
limitation: Bob's project-access entitlement is not independently shown; approved and explicitly shared items were not tested.

rationale: None of the required restriction is established. The guest list command returned no metadata, but the evidence does not establish that a sensitive item existed to be listed.
limitation: Access to the metadata of a known sensitive item by an author, reviewer, administrator, or unauthorized user was not observed.

rationale: The import command succeeded for a JSON source and reported two records imported, establishing import from one common document source.
limitation: Import from other common document sources was not tested.

rationale: The command reports importing two records from demo.json, but none of the required source types is established: the evidence does not identify it as a spreadsheet or a structured export from another requirements tool.
limitation: The source file’s format and provenance are not shown, so import from either stated source type remains untested.

rationale: No complete required behaviour is established. The command reports importing two items, but the recorded source is the same demo.json file used as the database; the evidence does not show that the items are policy or compliance references imported from an upstream repository.
limitation: The source's status as an upstream repository and the imported items' contents are unknown.

rationale: The import command completed and reported two items imported, but none of the required structure-preservation obligations is established by that acknowledgement.
limitation: No imported analysis was read back or inspected to verify preservation of goals, scenarios, requirements, policy links, or traceability.

rationale: The import completed and reported two records, but none of the required retention of classifications, tags, or version references was observed.
limitation: The evidence shows neither the source records' metadata nor the imported records, so retention of each metadata type remains untested.
